purpose: Classify the rounded rank-two residual by its exact conditional arithmetic content and prevent nearest-integer boundedness from being reported as an irrationality mechanism.

classification.recommended_terminology: rational-lattice divisibility screen for a nearest-integer linear form
classification.standard_mechanism: distance to the nearest integer on the lattice $(1/q)\mathbb Z$, together with coprimality of a reduced numerator and denominator
classification.attribution: Treat distance-to-the-nearest-integer and the rational lattice-spacing lemma as standard elementary Diophantine approximation. Attribute only the exact factorial-gap residual identity, determinant coefficient, and prime-unit translation architecture to the local Lean source.
classification.mathematical_interest: The generic lemma is routine. The valuable result is the exact semantic correction: conditional on $S=a/q$, strict rounded nonvanishing says $q\nmid\det A$ and nothing more unless an independent sub-lattice smallness estimate is supplied.
classification.reusable_scope: Any construction producing $NS+K$ with $N,K\in\mathbb Z$ and then translating to a nearest integer. The interpretation applies only after declaring a reduced rational representation $S=a/q$.
classification.why_it_matters: It stops a bounded residual from being mistaken for a Diophantine contradiction and relocates the #68 rank-two construction into the live denominator-smoothness lane, where its determinant can be compared with existing factorial divisibility exclusions.

primary_sources.title: An Introduction to Diophantine Approximation
primary_sources.author: J. W. S. Cassels
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Chapter I develops the one-dimensional distance-to-the-nearest-integer framework used throughout classical Diophantine approximation.
primary_sources.supports: Canonical terminology and context for $\|x\|$ as distance to the nearest integer and for comparing a linear form with its underlying rational lattice.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The factorial-gap residual, its Cramer determinant, or any #68-specific divisibility conclusion.

mechanism_comparison.nearest_integer_bound: For every real $x$, $\|x\|\le1/2$; this is normalization, not decay.
mechanism_comparison.rational_lattice: If $S=a/q$ is reduced, then $NS+K$ lies in $(1/q)\mathbb Z$ and its nearest-integer residual is zero exactly when $q\mid N$.
mechanism_comparison.genuine_irrationality_form: A rationality contradiction would need a nonzero residual strictly below $1/q$, or another independent argument incompatible with the lattice.
mechanism_comparison.source_specific_consumer: The Lean source supplies $N=\det A$ and an integral translation direction; it does not supply cofinal strict nonvanishing or sub-lattice smallness.

disconfirmation_search.result: The surrounding notation and lattice viewpoint are standard Diophantine approximation. No independent theorem-level novelty remains in the generic lemma; the only substantive classification task is the exact source-specific conditional interpretation.
disconfirmation_search.boundary: The citation establishes standard context, not a claim that Cassels states this factorial-gap specialization.

claim_boundary.allowed_wording: If the factorial-gap series is $S=a/q$ in lowest terms, then strict nonvanishing of the rounded Cramer residual is exactly the conditional divisibility exclusion $q\nmid\det A$; the universal $1/2$ nearest-integer bound is compatible with rationality and supplies no irrationality contradiction.
forbidden_wording: The rounded residual unconditionally excludes denominators.
A nonzero residual bounded by one half proves irrationality.
The construction gives a lower bound on q.
The source proves strict nonvanishing cofinally.
The Cramer determinant supplies a sub-lattice small linear form.
